stem: The table shows the results of a swimming test taken by the students at two schools. Which of the following statements is true?

choices.A: A randomly selected student from School Q is more likely to have passed than a randomly selected student from School P.
choices.B: A randomly selected student from School P is more likely to have passed than a randomly selected student from School Q.
choices.C: A randomly selected student who passed is more likely to be from School P than from School Q.
choices.D: A randomly selected student from School P and a randomly selected student from School Q are equally likely to have passed.

solution: \(0.70 > 0.68\), so a student from School P is more likely to have passed.
Among the 186 students who passed, 102 are from School Q, so statement D is false.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This compares the numbers of students who passed (\(102 > 84\)) instead of the probabilities; School Q also has more students.
explanation.B: Correct. The probability of passing is \(\frac{84}{120} = 0.70\) at School P and \(\frac{102}{150} = 0.68\) at School Q, and \(0.70 > 0.68\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. Of the \(84 + 102 = 186\) students who passed, only 84 are from School P, so a student who passed is more likely to be from School Q.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The probabilities are close (0.70 and 0.68) but not equal; this is the result of rounding too early.
